thread:
elaine-finance: FYI vendor invoice (SWI consulting) just arrived for LU entity. They stamped 15% withholding on the invoice and asked us to gross-up. Invoice also missing a VAT ID. Anyone handle Swiss vendor withholding rules?

mattie-legal: Quick Q — who is the billed entity? Redwood US or Redwood EU BV (Lux)? treaty implications differ.

elaine-finance: billed to Redwood EU BV (Luxembourg). contract SOW is services (integration work).

sanjay-ops: TL;DR: if vendor is Swiss and customer is LU entity, WHT might apply under LU domestic rules or via DTA. We usually ask for Certificate of Fiscal Residence from the vendor and then determine treaty rate. We don't auto-gross-up unless contractually agreed.

ivan-vendor: Hi — Ivan from SWI consulting. We can provide a CFR. We flagged 15% because local Swiss tax advisor recommended withholding when billing LU. We can reissue invoice grossed-up or provide net + WHT line. Which do you prefer?

mattie-legal: Provide CFR first. Also we need to check the Luxembourg–Switzerland DTA: some service categories have 0% withholding, others subject to reduced rates. I’ll look up the exact article.

tax-bot: Reminder: W-8/W-9 are for US payees only. For Swiss payees, Finance needs a Certificate of Tax Residence (CFR) and any DTA forms required by Luxembourg for reduced/zero WHT. Send to finance@redwood.com.

elaine-finance: Ok I'll ask vendor for CFR + a revised invoice that clearly shows: gross amount, WHT amount (if they want net), and a note whether they request gross-up. Holding payment until docs received.

ivan-vendor: Sending CFR + new invoice in ~45m. If Redwood prefers we can show both variants on invoice (gross and net) to make accounting easier.

sanjay-ops: Action item: Elaine to confirm with vendor whether they want us to withhold and remit or for us to gross-up. If they want gross-up, procurement + finance approval needed (cost increases). If withholding, we need CFR and we’ll apply the treaty rate once legal confirms.

mattie-legal: I’ll confirm treaty position by EOD. Note: sometimes LU requires a Luxembourg tax clearance to apply reduced treaty rates — will check.

elaine-finance: Thanks. Adding #procure and #tax channels if we need signoff. Pinging @ivan-vendor when docs arrive.

ivan-vendor: Sent CFR and invoice v2 (attached). Invoice v2 has a line: "Service fee 30,000 EUR — Withholding 4,500 EUR (15%) — Net due 25,500 EUR". Also included a note requesting gross-up if possible.

mattie-legal: Got it. I’m checking the DTA now. If Luxembourg-Schweiz treaty gives 0% for this service we will request refund/relief; otherwise finance will withhold at treaty or domestic rate.

elaine-finance: Understood. Holding payment until we have confirmation. If gross-up required by vendor, I'll open a PO change request.

sanjay-ops: One more ops note — please ensure vendor's invoice includes their bank details and tax reg number for our AP payment file.

elaine-finance: Will do. Thanks all :handshake:

tax-bot: Note added to thread: "Documentation required for non‑US vendors: Certificate of Fiscal Residence, updated invoice showing WHT, vendor bank details."
